title: [Performance][MoE] Optimize NPU event recording for MoE multistream overlap
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? The NPU events recorded around the routed-experts path (router milestones `shared_input_ready`/`router_output_ready`, and `before_dispatch`/`before_gmm2`/`before_combine` inside the routed path) are consumed **only** by the shared-expert side stream, which exists solely when `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` is enabled. When the overlap is off, every `record_event` is pure host-side overhead paid per MoE layer per step, and host-side record is notably slow. The consumers in `shared_experts.py` already gate every wait on the same flag (`_wait_for_milestone` returns immediately when the overlap is off and fails fast if a milestone is missing while it is on), and the `RoutedMoEMilestones`/`FusedExpertsResult` event fields are already `Optional`. So the producer-side records can be skipped safely with no consumer changes. This PR gates the always-on-path record sites behind the flag via a shared helper, `maybe_record_event()` (defined in `ops/fused_moe/moe_mlp.py`): - `ops/fused_moe/moe_mlp.py`: define `maybe_record_event()` and use it for the `before_gmm2_evt` record in `apply_moe_mlp`; the entry now returns an Optional event; - `ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py`: gate `before_dispatch_evt` / `before_combine_evt`; - `ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`: gate `shared_input_ready` / `router_output_ready` in `_prepare_router_and_milestones` (`routed_finalize_done` is already recorded only on the SP-overlap gather path, so it needs no extra gating). `maybe_record_event()` skips the record only when the initialized config proves the overlap is off; an uninitialized config keeps the legacy always-record behavior. The 310P-specific and LoRA gmm2 records are intentionally left unconditional for now (not yet validated on device); they can adopt the same gate in a follow-up. With the overlap off (default), the main MoE path no longer issues any event records; with the overlap on, behavior is unchanged. ### Profiling Host-side timeline of one MoE layer step before and after this change: **Before (events recorded unconditionally on the routed stream):** **After (records skipped when multistream overlap is off):** ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. With `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` enabled the behavior is unchanged; with it disabled only the unused event records are skipped. ### How was this patch tested? - The runner-contract unit tests (`tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py`) patch the overlap flag explicitly to keep exercising the record path, and new cases cover the skip path (milestones stay `None` with `record_event` never called); all other MoE tests (including 310P and LoRA) run unchanged. - CPU UT / pre-commit / DCO checks on this PR. - E2E MoE serving on Ascend NPU with `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` off (skip path) and on (unchanged path), plus the profiling screenshots above. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607
